rationale: Ground truth is thin (LGTM plus four style/organization nits on patch.py relevance and move-to-utils requests); neither candidate addresses those specific points, so recall is near-zero for both (X gets marginal credit for engaging the same benchmarks/patch.py hunk with a different critique). Both independently converge on the same real, well-evidenced bug (double-seeded num_stale_output_tokens) and the same arg_utils.py unconditional-registration regression, which is strong cross-corroboration for precision on their headline findings. X is better organized and more actionable (Blocking/Should-fix/Minor buckets, concrete diffs, suggested tests) but its narrative 'reproduced' terminal output is unverifiable and slightly risks fabrication; Y's grep/quote-backed evidence per finding is more auditable and surfaces one unique, concrete bug (NPU _dummy_run kwarg mismatch) but its dense sweep-dump format is harder to act on directly.
